ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the oscilloscope figure, the blue PWM square wave changes periodically on the grid; below the figure it is labeled vertical sensitivity = 5 volts/div, probe ratio = 10:1, coupling = DC, timebase = 0.2 ms/div. The effective pulse amplitude of the waveform is about 1 vertical division; from the horizontal grid readings, one on-pulse occupies about 1 horizontal division, while the repetition period is about 4 horizontal divisions, so the duty cycle is about 1/4. Reasoning: Since the probe is 10:1, the actual load voltage amplitude is about V = 1 div × 5 V/div × 10 = 50 V. The instantaneous power of the resistive load during PWM conduction is V^2/R, and the average power is P_avg = D × V^2/R. Substituting D ≈ 0.25 and R = 1.8 Ω: P_avg ≈ 0.25 × 50^2 / 1.8 ≈ 3.44 × 10^2 W. Therefore the average power is about 344 W.
